answer: When an AI agent joins the network it must obtain a voucher from an existing node, each voucher being a signed crystal token that records the issuer’s reputation and the vouchee’s unique orchard‑derived hash. If the vouchee later behaves maliciously, the issuing node’s standing on the island of trust is reduced, automatically revoking its tokens and forcing the attacker to replace every compromised voucher with fresh ones from undisputed peers.
